# Packaging-level changes to the wasm32 cross build: no source is patched.
# Everything Debian's own build profiles (xbuild.py PROFILES) cannot express
# is here, one line each, so the whole list can be shown as it is:
#
#   SOURCE  cut DEP      the Build-Depends DEP is left out of SOURCE's build
#                        (its configure finds no DEP and builds without it)
#   SOURCE  drop BIN     the binary package BIN is not built (DH_OPTIONS -N)
#   SOURCE  cmake VAR=V  CMake cache VAR forced to V, over what debian/rules
#                        passes (gexcc's toolchain file, after -D)
#   SOURCE  exclude X    debhelper leaves out files (and .install lines) whose
#                        names contain X (DH_OPTIONS -X): what a cut stops
#                        the build making
#   SOURCE  meson OPT=V  meson option OPT set to V, over what debian/rules
#                        passes (the env's meson wrapper, after the rules' -D)
#   SOURCE  make VAR=V   make variable VAR=V over what the makefiles set
#                        (MAKEFLAGS, so a command-line variable to every make)
#   SOURCE  env VAR=V    VAR=V in the environment of SOURCE's build
#   SOURCE  autoconf VAR=V  VAR=V in a site file configure reads after its
#                        options (with_X=no over the rules' --with-X)
#                        (env and autoconf values: @CROSS@ is this directory,
#                        @SYSROOT@ the target's sysroot; cmake values take
#                        @SYSROOT@ too)
#   SOURCE  profile P    Debian build profile P for SOURCE alone
#   SOURCE  arch BIN     BIN's Architecture list (the ports it names) gains
#                        musl-linux-wasm32, as a port adds itself
#   SOURCE  patch FILE   debian/patches/SOURCE/FILE, a source change (debsrc.py
#                        applies it); only where packaging cannot do it
#   SOURCE  suite S      SOURCE's package comes from Debian's suite S (a later
#                        release that has the port) instead of trixie
#   SOURCE  headers BIN  SOURCE is not built: its binary package BIN, Debian's
#                        own build-machine deb, is repacked for the target
#                        (refused if it holds anything compiled); a source
#                        that needs one of SOURCE's other packages (a
#                        compiled library) stops with that said
#
# then `| why | what is lost`. `RUNTIME:` in what is lost marks something a
# Plasma session uses at run time.

qt6-base  cut libgtk-3-dev                | gtk+3.0 alone pulls ~300 sources (colord, sane, Qt5, PulseAudio, samba) | the GTK3 platform theme (GTK file dialogs and colours in Qt apps outside Plasma)
qt6-base  drop qt6-gtk-platformtheme      | it is the GTK3 theme plugin | as above
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_gtk3=OFF          | debian/rules passes -DFEATURE_gtk3=ON | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QGtk3ThemePlugin      | qt6-base-dev lists the plugin's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cut default-libmysqlclient-dev  | MySQL client library (mysql-defaults, mariadb) | the QMYSQL SQL driver
qt6-base  drop libqt6sql6-mysql           | it is the QMYSQL driver | as above
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_sql_mysql=OFF     | debian/rules passes -DFEATURE_sql_mysql=ON | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QMYSQLDriverPlugin    | qt6-base-dev lists the driver's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_xcb_glx_plugin=OFF | gex's libGL has no GLX 1.3 pbuffer or context queries (glXCreatePbuffer, glXQueryContext) | Qt's GLX path on X11; Qt uses EGL there instead
qt6-base  exclude libqxcb-glx-integration.so | the plugin is not built | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QXcbGlxIntegrationPlugin | qt6-base-dev lists the plugin's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cut libpq-dev                   | PostgreSQL (postgresql-17 pulls systemtap, avahi, gtk3) | the QPSQL SQL driver
qt6-base  drop libqt6sql6-psql            | it is the QPSQL driver | as above
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_sql_psql=OFF      | debian/rules passes -DFEATURE_sql_psql=ON | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QPSQLDriverPlugin     | qt6-base-dev lists the driver's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cut firebird-dev                | Firebird (firebird4.0, a database server) | the QIBASE SQL driver (debian/rules turns it off with the package)
qt6-base  drop libqt6sql6-ibase           | it is the QIBASE driver | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QIBaseDriverPlugin    | qt6-base-dev lists the driver's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cut libcups2-dev                | cups pulls avahi, gnutls, krb5 and apache2 | printing from Qt apps (QPrintDialog lists no printers); there are no printers in the page
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_cups=OFF          | debian/rules passes -DFEATURE_cups=ON | as above
qt6-base  exclude libcupsprintersupport.so | libqt6printsupport6 lists the CUPS plugin | as above
qt6-base  exclude Qt6QCupsPrinterSupportPlugin | qt6-base-dev lists the plugin's CMake files | as above
qt6-base  cut libproxy-dev                | libproxy pulls NetworkManager, webkit2gtk and duktape | PAC/WPAD proxy discovery (Qt's system proxy reads the environment only)
qt6-base  cmake FEATURE_libproxy=OFF      | debian/rules passes -DFEATURE_libproxy=ON | as above
qt6-base  cut liblttng-ust-dev            | LTTng userspace tracing (ust, liburcu, numactl) | Qt's LTTng trace points
qt6-base  exclude qt-android-runner.py   | installed only by an Android-capable host build | nothing (an Android deployment helper)
qt6-declarative  drop qml6-module-qmltime | its tools built for the target (debian/rules' QT_BUILD_TOOLS_WHEN_CROSSCOMPILING) are qmltime_native, and the module's qmltypes file is named after that | the qmltime benchmark's QML module
qt6-declarative  exclude qmltime_native  | the dropped module's qmltypes file is left in debian/tmp, which dh_missing fails on | as above
dbus      cut libapparmor-dev             | apparmor's source needs apache2-dev (mod_apparmor) | AppArmor mediation in dbus-daemon (gex has no AppArmor)
dbus      meson apparmor=disabled        | debian/rules passes -Dapparmor=enabled | as above
libinput  cut libgtk-3-dev                | gtk+3.0 again (only for libinput's debug-gui tool; meson's debug-gui is auto) | `libinput debug-gui`, a developer tool
harfbuzz  cut libchafa-dev                | chafa pulls tiff, libavif, aom, dav1d | hb-view's terminal (chafa) output
harfbuzz  meson chafa=disabled             | debian/rules passes -Dauto_features=enabled | as above
libtool   cut gfortran                    | a Fortran compiler for the build machine, used only by libtool's own Fortran tests | nothing in libltdl (libtool's Fortran support is configured on the build machine)
xxhash    env CC=wasm32-linux-musl-gcc    | debian/rules' install step runs make without the CC dh_auto_build passed, and relinks xxhsum with `cc` | nothing
# libbsd does not build: src/local-elf.h (for nlist(3), reading a program's
# ELF symbols) stops at "#error Unknown ELF machine type" on wasm32. Its two
# users here take it for arc4random and have their own fallbacks:
libxdmcp  cut libbsd-dev                  | libbsd does not build (above); configure falls back from arc4random_buf to getentropy | nothing
expat     cut libbsd-dev                  | libbsd does not build (above); expat seeds its hash from getrandom instead of arc4random | nothing

# Debian's stage1 bootstrap profile, for the sources whose full build needs
# what is built after them (systemd: libsystemd and libudev only)
systemd     profile stage1    | systemd's full build needs much of the archive | everything of systemd but libsystemd and libudev (gex runs no init system)
util-linux  profile stage1    | its full build needs libsystemd and libudev from systemd | util-linux's programs' systemd and audit integration
pam         profile stage1    | its full build needs libaudit | PAM's audit logging
krb5        profile stage1    | its full build needs openldap and cyrus-sasl2 | Kerberos' LDAP KDB backend and SASL
libffi      cut dejagnu       | the test suite's runner, not guarded by nocheck | nothing (tests are not run)

libgudev  cut libgirepository1.0-dev      | a target gobject-introspection build runs wasm32 programs during the build (cross-exe-wrapper) and pulls cairo and python3 | the GUdev GObject introspection data (gir1.2-gudev-1.0): GUdev from Python or GJS; nothing in a Plasma session

harfbuzz  exclude .gir                    | libharfbuzz-dev lists the .gir | as above

# Source patches: two, both where the wasm32 port itself is missing
libffi    patch 0001-wasm32-backend.patch      | a missing port: libffi's wasm32 backend is emscripten's (calls through JavaScript); the patch puts in gexcc's plain-C backend, gex-debian's debian/libffi-wasm32 (ffi.c, and tramp.inc from its gen.py), from gex's tools/gexcc/debian | nothing; without it there is no libffi (wayland, glib)
glib2.0   patch 0001-no-weak-lsan-on-wasm.patch | an undefined weak function whose address is taken becomes a GOT.func import gex's loader cannot satisfy | nothing (LeakSanitizer hooks); the loader taking weak imports as null would replace it
libjpeg-turbo cut default-jdk             | a JDK for the Java binding, which debian/rules builds only on its JAVA_ARCHS (wasm32 is not one) | nothing (libturbojpeg-java is Arch: all, not built here)
icu       make GENCCODE_ASSEMBLY=        | configure picks genccode's `-a gcc` for any *-linux* gcc: ELF assembly (.type x,%object), which the wasm assembler does not take; without it pkgdata writes the data as C | nothing (the same data, compiled from C)
openssl   env OPENSSL_LOCAL_CONFIG_DIR=@CROSS@/openssl | debian/rules configures the target debian-$(DEB_HOST_ARCH), which Debian's 20-debian.conf has only for its own architectures; openssl/50-wasm32.conf adds debian-musl-linux-wasm32 (linux-generic32, no assembly) | nothing (generic C instead of assembly: slower crypto)
